summary: LUNAR QUEST is an online browser game where kids ages 7 to 12 step into a lunar rover cockpit at the Moon's south pole. Facing real world challenges inspired by NASA's Artemis missions, players use a simple four step method to handle space emergencies like solar radiation, dust buildup and air pressure issues. By turning difficult aerospace science into fun, interactive gameplay, the project makes space exploration exciting and accessible for young learners.
details:
LUNAR QUEST is an interactive, browser playable lunar rover cockpit simulator for kids ages 7–12. It translates NASA lunar south pole research into a clean, minimalist UI with zero gauge clutter. Players tackle five NASA engineering missions such as solar radiation alerts and dust shielding through a simple 4 step mission loop. It sparks early interest in STEM and space exploration.

Project Details

  • What it does & how it works: Simulates a 1st-person lunar rover cockpit at Shackleton Crater. Players manage outpost emergencies via a 4-step loop: Briefing > Investigation > Interactive Fix > NASA Science Lesson. Missions include solar radiation, lunar dust, air valves, hull breaches and airlock safety.
  • Benefits & Impact: Zero barrier accessibility with no downloads or logins required. It optimizes cognitive load for children ages 7–12 to spark early interest in STEM and Artemis missions.
  • Tools & Tech Used: Built using React, Type Script, and Tailwind CSS via Lovable. Research and workflow guidance was structured using Google Gemini, drawing from official NASA Artemis, HRP, LRO and engineering history.
  • Creativity & Design: Gamifies real historical Apollo and ISS engineering anomalies into tactile, kid-friendly interactions inside a cinematic cockpit view, balancing scientific accuracy with rapid hackathon execution.
